Which countries have won the most medals at the Summer Olympics? Updating the tally before Paris 2024 | NBC Olympics [ Skip to main content ](https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/which-countries-have-won-most-medals-summer-olympics-updating-tally-paris-2024#main-content)
The 30th edition of the Summer Olympic Games is about to kick off in Paris. These Games feature 10,500 athletes competing for 206 National Olympic Committees (NOCs), plus a Refugee Olympic Team.
So, before those 206 nations vie for medals starting on July 24, it's time to check in on the latest all-time medal count at the Summer Games.
## 
Which country has the most medals from the Summer Olympics?
The United States leads the way with 2,643 total medals, 1,521 more than any other nation. The Soviet Union is in second place with 1,122 medals, followed by Great Britain (915).
## 
Which country has the most gold medals from the Summer Olympics?
Again, the U.S. reigns supreme, with 1,065 gold medals. The Soviet Union trails in second place with 440 golds.
## 
Which country won the most medals at the Tokyo Olympics?
The U.S. led the charge with 113 total medals in Tokyo, followed by China, with 89, and the Russian Olympic Committee with 71. The 39 gold medals for the U.S. also ranked first, barely edging China’s 38 golds.
## 
Which athlete has the most medals in Summer Olympics history?
That honor belongs to U.S. swimming legend **Michael Phelps**. Phelps' 28 medals — including 23 golds — stands as an Olympic record. Phelps also was the first athlete to win eight gold medals at a single Olympic Games, which he accomplished at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
Soviet gymnast **Larisa** **Latynina** has the second-most of all-time, with 18 medals (nine golds).
